title: What a Dog Smells in Another Dog's Scent
topic: Why do dogs sniff each other's butts?

beats.label: the nose knows
lines: Your dog's nose is forty times more sensitive than yours.
The special scents they use for communication are called pheromones.

beats.title: A chemical signature
lines: Here's the twist: a dog's anal gland gives its droppings a particular signature.
It identifies which dog it was, and where the dung was left.

beats.title: What scent reveals
lines: Some chemical signatures reveal a dog's sex and age, and whether a female is pregnant or recently gave birth.
Different hormones are even released when a dog is angry, fearful or confident.
Many of those chemicals dissolve in urine.
So sniffing where another dog has peed tells a dog a great deal about that dog.
So on your next walk, let your dog sniff a little longer: it's learning who passed by.

sources.claim: Dogs have an olfactory sense 40 times more sensitive than a human's; the special scents dogs use for communication are called pheromones.
The anal gland of canines gives a particular signature to fecal deposits and identifies the marker as well as the place where the dung is left.
Different hormones are secreted when a dog is angry, fearful or confident; chemical signatures identify sex, age, and whether a female is in estrus, pregnant or recently gave birth.
Many pheromone chemicals are dissolved in urine, and sniffing where another dog has urinated gives a dog a great deal of information about that dog.
